messages.subject: tangled in Git again
parts:
OK, I ran into another Git SNAFU working on the
branch

bugfix/issue-464-diag_pre_multiply

which branched from

hotfix/v2.1.1


Somehow the test rug got pulled out from under my feet and
I'm going to need help getting myself out of this mess.

I've attached the new test, which is the only thing I was
trying to add at this juncture. The good news is the
test works. The bad news is I have no friggin' clue what
to do from here. Here's what happened in case that helps.

I added the test locally and committed it, no problem.

~/stan(bugfix/issue-464-diag_pre_multiply)$ git commit -a -m "added and verified a thorough diag_post_multiply test"
[bugfix/issue-464-diag_pre_multiply f24c9dd] added and verified a thorough diag_post_multiply test
1 file changed, 316 insertions(+), 823 deletions(-)
rewrite src/test/agrad/fwd/matrix/diag_post_multiply_test.cpp (98%)


Then I tried to push, but no luck.


~/stan(bugfix/issue-464-diag_pre_multiply)$ git push
To https://github.com/stan-dev/stan.git
! [rejected] bugfix/issue-464-diag_pre_multiply -> bugfix/issue-464-diag_pre_multiply (fetch first)
error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/stan-dev/stan.git'
hint: Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do
hint: not have locally. This is usually caused by another repository pushing
hint: to the same ref. You may want to first merge the remote changes (e.g.,
hint: 'git pull') before pushing again.
hint: See the 'Note about fast-forwards' in 'git push --help' for details.


So, I tried to pull hotfix/v2.1.1 from origin

~/stan(bugfix/issue-464-diag_pre_multiply)$ git pull origin hotfix/v2.1.1

and all hell broke loose. Now I'm going to need help figuring out where
to go from here. Below is what I got after running the above (and below that, what I
got from running "git status"

- Bob

So I didn't see the output from git status, but I'm guessing you have some conflicts?  At the very least I'm pretty certain you still won't be able to push.

Anyway, I think the issue is that you actually needed to do a:

git pull origin bugfix/issue-464-diag_pre_multiply

(or, probably equivalently just git pull)

I'm not sure the best way to fix it.  I think you need to do a:

git reset --hard YOURCOMMIT

where YOURCOMMIT is the commit with the test before you did the git pull.  Then do the git pull from the bugfix branch and you should be good to go.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] tangled in Git again
parts:
Bob, I fixed the branch and included your test.

Thanks, Marcus. I always forget how to do that.
On Thu, Jan 30, 2014 at 11:45 AM, Marcus Brubaker <marcus.a...@gmail.com> wrote:

So I didn't see the output from git status, but I'm guessing you have some conflicts?  At the very least I'm pretty certain you still won't be able to push.

Anyway, I think the issue is that you actually needed to do a:

git pull origin bugfix/issue-464-diag_pre_multiply

(or, probably equivalently just git pull)

I'm not sure the best way to fix it.  I think you need to do a:

git reset --hard YOURCOMMIT

where YOURCOMMIT is the commit with the test before you did the git pull.  Then do the git pull from the bugfix branch and you should be good to go.

Cheers,
Marcus



On Thu, Jan 30, 2014 at 10:32 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
OK, I ran into another Git SNAFU working on the
branch

   bugfix/issue-464-diag_pre_multiply

which branched from

  hotfix/v2.1.1


Somehow the test rug got pulled out from under my feet and
I'm going to need help getting myself out of this mess.

I've attached the new test, which is the only thing I was
trying to add at this juncture.  The good news is the
test works.  The bad news is I have no friggin' clue what
to do from here.  Here's what happened in case that helps.

I added the test locally and committed it, no problem.

>

> Cheers,
> Marcus
